cards.name: Topic marker
cards.fn: Sets what the sentence is about: “as for this…”
cards.picture: a spotlight on the word before it.
cards.en: As for me, I'm a student.

cards.name: Subject marker
cards.fn: Points out who or what does something, often as new information.

cards.name: Object marker
cards.fn: Marks what the verb acts on.
cards.picture: an arrow from the verb to its target.

cards.name: Destination and point
cards.fn: Marks a destination, a point in time, or where something exists.
cards.picture: a pin dropped on a map.

cards.name: Place of action and means
cards.fn: Marks where an action happens or what you use to do it.
cards.picture: a stage with the action on it, or a tool in your hand.

cards.name: Direction
cards.picture: a compass needle swinging toward a place.

cards.name: Linker
cards.fn: Links two nouns, like “my” or “of”. The first noun describes the second.
cards.picture: a chain link joining two boxes.

cards.name: Also
cards.fn: Means “also” or “too”, and takes the place of は, が, or を.
cards.picture: a plus sign adding one more to the group.
cards.en: My friend is a student too.

cards.name: “With” or “and”
cards.fn: Means “with” a partner, or “and” between nouns.

items.note: School is the destination. へ also works here.

why.を: を marks what a verb acts on. School is where you're heading, not a target of 行きます.
why.と: と means “with” a partner. You aren't going together with the school.

items.note: Studying is an action, and school is where it happens.

why.を: を would make school the subject you're studying.
why.に: に marks a destination or where something exists. For the place of an action, use で.

items.note: 学校 describes which kind of teacher.

why.を: を needs a verb to act on it. Here there are two nouns to link.
why.で: で marks the place of an action, and being a teacher here describes the noun 先生.

items.note: The friend is your conversation partner.

why.を: を would make the friend the thing being spoken, as if you were saying them aloud.
why.で: で marks a place or means. A friend isn't where or how you talk.

items.note: The friend does the coming, and is new information.

why.を: を marks the object, but the friend is the one who comes.
why.で: で marks a place or means, not who does the action.

items.en: My friend is also a student.
items.note: The English says “also”, so も fits.

why.は: は is grammatical, but it only sets the topic. It loses the “also”.
why.を: を marks the object of a verb. です doesn't take an object.

items.note: へ stresses the direction. に also works here.

why.を: を marks what a verb acts on. Japan is where you're heading.
why.が: が would make Japan the one doing the going.

items.note: “As for” signals the topic of the sentence.

why.を: を needs an action verb. きれいです describes rather than acts.
why.で: で marks the place of an action, and nothing is being done here.

why.を: を needs a verb to act on it, and 日本 and 山 are both nouns.
why.へ: へ marks direction of movement, and nothing is moving here.

items.note: The book is what reading acts on.

why.が: が would make the book the one doing the reading.
why.へ: へ marks direction of movement, and reading isn't movement.

items.note: 好き is an adjective in Japanese, so what you like takes が.

why.を: を marks the object of a verb, but 好き is an adjective.
why.で: で marks a place or means. Books aren't the means of liking.

items.note: The book is the tool you study with.

why.へ: へ marks direction of movement, and studying isn't movement.
why.と: と means “with” a partner. For a tool, use で.
